narrative:
The model predicts you have a 36% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to help you succeed.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key factors in your profile. By far the strongest influence is your history of three past class failures. While students who passed had zero previous failures on average, your record of repeated setbacks strongly pushed the model toward expecting you to fail again.

The second most important factor is that you are receiving extra educational support at school. This actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward passing, because the model has learned that students getting this kind of help tend to improve their chances.

Third, having your father as guardian also nudged the prediction slightly toward passing. Most students who succeed have their mother as guardian, so your situation is less common among those who pass, but it still had a modest positive effect.

To improve, focus first on breaking the cycle of failure. With only 2–5 hours of weekly study time and no internet at home, you may benefit from using the remedial courses to build stronger study habits, seek consistent help early, and protect time for schoolwork. Addressing these areas now gives you the best chance to turn the prediction around before final exams. (248 words)
